question: What conspicuity treatment is labeled 'E' in Figure 2A-1?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In Figure 2A-1, item "E" is a **vertical retroreflective strip on the sign support**. The figure illustrates it with a fluorescent yellow-green pedestrian crossing (W11-2) sign and diagonal arrow plaque, where a retroreflective strip is applied vertically along the sign post, extending down to a maximum of 2 feet above the ground/edge-of-pavement level. This is one of the optional methods for enhancing the conspicuity of a standard sign. Options (permitted): - "Based upon engineering judgment, where the improvement of the conspicuity of a standard regulatory, warning, or guide sign is desired, any of the following methods may be used, as appropriate, to enhance the sign's conspicuity (see Figure 2A-1)…" — Figure 2A-1's labeled examples include "E – Vertical retroreflective strip" on sign support, among the conspicuity treatments referenced by this Option provision. Visual evidence: [Image 1] (Figure 2A-1, p.48) shows item E labeled "Vertical retroreflective strip on sign support," depicting a pedestrian crossing warning sign assembly with a yellow-green retroreflective strip running vertically along the post, dimensioned "2 ft MAX." from the bottom of the strip to the ground line. [Image 2] (Page 89) shows the same Figure 2A-1 in full-page context, confirming item E as the vertical retroreflective strip treatment with the 2 ft MAX. dimension. [Image 3], [Image 4], and [Image 5] show other figures (colored pavement applications, sign heights/lateral locations, and tubular markers) and are not directly relevant to item E. Citations: - Section 2A.11 Option §1 (p.49) - Figure 2A-1 (p.48) - Page 89
gold_answer: A vertical retroreflective strip on the sign support.
